newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai rubber steady to lower, govt seeking stocks.
newsitem.headline: Thai rubber steady to lower, govt seeking stocks.

text.p: Thai rubber prices were steady to lower on Wednesday with the government still negotiating prices for 5,000 tonnes of RSS3 rubber it intended to buy, trade sources said.

The government entered the market on Friday to make inquiries for the rubber. But so far the offered prices were higher than the 117 US cents per kg sought by the government, the sources told Reuters.
"The lowest offered prices still stand at 120 cents a kg," said an official at the Hat Yai-based rubber auction market.
The market was confused by news from Tokyo quoting a Thai deputy minister as saying that the government would refrain from buying RSS3.

"I don't know which statement I should base my decision on. The government had earlier said repeatedly that they will buy a big amount to prop up prices. Now they said they won't. Are they serious?," said one Bangkok-based trader.
Thai Deputy Agriculture Minister Grich Gongpechara said in Tokyo that the government would not be buying more rubber for the time being.
"This could affect those holding long positions,' said another trader.
However, the news had limited immediate impact on rubber prices. Overall weak demand remained a major factor that depressed the market, traders said.
"Stocks are still a big problem. The demand is really slow. There have been some inquiries this week but no deal was heard so far," said the Bangkok trader.
Traders said, however, the downside for rubber prices was limited mostly because of higher Tokyo prices.
The benchmark RSS3 rubber was indicated around 117.00-118.00 US cents a kg FOB Bangkok on Wednesday but traders said some shippers refused to sell below 118 cents.
Concentrated latex was quoted around 90 cent a kg on the same basis.
